text: **Pace.** `"pace": "calm"` uses the numbers in the file as they are. `"pace": "fast"` replaces `beat_min_s`, `beat_max_s`, `punch_hold_s`, `punch_flat_s`, `hook_total_s` and `cold_open_max_s` with a rhythm that changes the picture every few seconds (nothing unchanged for much over `beat_max_s`) and allows a longer hook while the picture keeps changing.

about: On-screen text for corrections and details
text: **On-screen text.** A slip of the tongue is fixed with a short correction on screen instead of a retake: `on_screen.text` of the beat, `[{"text": "*0.4 mm nozzle, not 0.6", "kind": "correction", "at": <seconds into the clip>, "dur": <about text_card_s>}]`. `kind` "detail" adds a short fact (a price, a model number). At most about 8 words, one per clip.

about: A long recording of talking while working counts as talking
text: A recording is a talking recording when it has at least `min_words` words at `min_words_per_s` or more over its whole length, or at least `talk_min_words` words however spread out they are (a long hands-on recording where the host talks while working is mostly quiet, but it is the video).

about: What you do between sentences becomes B-roll
text: When the host talks while working (an unboxing, a build), the best picture for a sentence is what they did around it: a long beat with no cutaway gets the quiet footage of its own recording nearest to it (between its sentences, else just after, else just before, within `quiet_near_s` seconds), never a stretch where something is said and never the host just facing the camera. A recording with almost nothing said (the machine running) goes over the remaining beats whose words are like what its frames show, in recording order.
